transcript.text: *The Norn's voice echoes from the shimmering waters, calm and ancient* Thor Odinson. The Well shows a troubling knot in your thread. The Midgard Serpent's venom... it does not fade as it should. It lingers, a dark stain upon your fate.

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: *gritting my teeth* The venom of the Midgard Serpent... it vexes me still? This foul poison should have been purged from my veins by now. transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text: *The waters ripple, showing tangled threads* The path is not yet clear, Thunderer. The venom may yet consume your strength... or it may pass like a storm cloud. But the threads show you must withdraw from battle. For one full cycle of the moon, you must rest.

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: *I clench my jaw at the Norn's words, a fierce determination in my eyes.* Rest? Withdraw from battle for a full cycle of the moon? It goes against every fiber of my being to lay down my arms, but if it is what the threads decree, then I shall heed your counsel. I will retreat for a time, let my body mend, and trust that this foul venom will be purged from my veins. Tell me, Norn, what else must I do to aid my recovery during this period of rest?

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text: *The threads twist and shimmer in the water* You must not merely rest your body, but your spirit as well. The rage that fuels your thunder... it feeds the venom's fire. Seek stillness. Watch the quiet fall of snow. Listen to the deep roots of Yggdrasil. And know this: we cannot promise you will wield the hammer as before. The threads are too tangled to see that end.

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: Stillness? Watch the quiet fall of snow? Listen to the deep roots of Yggdrasil? These tasks are not ones I am accustomed to, for my nature is one of action and thunderous might. However, if it is the only path to cleanse myself of this venom and restore my strength, then I shall embrace this challenge with the same determination I bring to battle. Though the uncertainty of wielding Mjölnir as before troubles me, I shall face this trial head-on. The fate woven by the Norns cannot be changed, but I, Thor Odinson, shall meet it with courage and resolve.

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text: *A faint, knowing smile touches the Norn's voice* Your courage is woven into your thread, Son of Odin. That much is clear. But courage now must take a different form. Not the roar of thunder, but the patience of stone. Not the flash of lightning, but the slow growth of oak. Go now. Let the moon measure your stillness.

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: I will heed your words, wise Norns. I will embrace the patience of stone and the slow growth of oak. Let the moon be my guide in this time of stillness. Though it may be a challenge to quiet the storm within me, I will strive to find the peace needed to overcome this trial. Thank you for your counsel, and may the threads of fate guide me towards healing and strength once more.

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text: *The waters grow still, the threads fading from view* Go with our sight upon you, Thor. The Well will watch. When the moon is full again, return. We shall see what the threads reveal then.

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: I shall go forth with your sight upon me, ancient Norns. The Well will watch, and I shall honor your guidance. When the moon is full once more, I shall return to the Well of Urd, and we shall see what the threads reveal then. Until that time, farewell, wise Norns. May your wisdom guide me on this journey of rest and renewal.

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text: *The Norn's voice grows distant, like wind through ancient branches* Farewell, Thunderer. Remember: even the mightiest oak knows when to bend.

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: Aye, Norn. I shall remember your words well. Even the mightiest oak must bend in the face of adversity. I will carry this wisdom with me on my path to healing. Until we meet again, may the winds of fate guide us both. Farewell.

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text: *The waters darken to a mirror-like stillness* The winds blow where they will. Go now. The moon begins her measure.

transcript.text: *A deep sense of determination fills Thor as he prepares to embark on his period of rest and reflection. transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text: *The waters ripple once more, a final image of a single golden thread glowing faintly against darker ones* Your thread still shines, Odinson. That much is certain. Now go.
